claims.explanation: Ouabain kills cancer cells by binding and inhibiting the Na+/K+-ATPase (ATP1A1), and selectivity likely arises from differential dependence on specific ATP1A1 isoforms and on HIF-1α, whose translation is blocked by cardiac glycosides. Lines with high ATP1A1 expression and/or HIF-1 pathway activation are expected to be most sensitive, while those with low ATP1A1 or high expression of ouabain-resistant ATP1A isoforms (e.g., ATP1A3) are protected.

features.basis: primary target of ouabain; higher expression increases binding and pump inhibition
cardiac glycosides inhibit HIF-1α synthesis; HIF-1-dependent tumors are more sensitive
alpha3 isoform has lower ouabain affinity and can substitute for inhibited alpha1
beta1 subunit is required for functional Na/K-ATPase; high expression may increase ouabain-sensitive pump complexes
TP53 mutations are enriched in sensitive lines, possibly reflecting altered stress responses
KRAS-mutant lines are enriched among sensitive lines, possibly via metabolic or HIF-1 dependence
BRAF-mutant lines (BCPAP, WM793, HEC265) appear in sensitive group
ARID1A mutations are common in sensitive lines, suggesting chromatin remodeling affects ouabain response
NF1 mutations appear in several sensitive lines, possibly via RAS pathway activation
SMARCA4 mutations are enriched in sensitive lines, implicating SWI/SNF in sensitivity
CDKN2A mutations are frequent in sensitive lines, possibly reflecting proliferative advantage
PTEN mutations appear in several resistant lines, suggesting PI3K/AKT activation may protect
